title: Vectorial bent functions admitting maximal-component extensions
summary: Classify which vectorial bent functions admit nontrivial square extensions with the maximum possible number of bent components.

formal_statement.body: Let $n=2m$ and let $B:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^m$ be vectorial bent. Give necessary and sufficient conditions for $B$ to admit a nontrivial extension $F:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^n$ having exactly $2^n-2^m$ bent components, and construct such an $F$ for every positive case. Nontriviality and extension are understood in the source sense.

scope.domain: Vectorial bent functions and square functions with the maximum number of bent components
assumptions: The extension is nontrivial in the source sense
The extension has exactly $2^n-2^m$ bent components
scope.unresolved_remainder: Published later work supplies generic constructions and several positive extension families, including functions beyond the Nyberg bound and families derived from Niho and Maiorana--McFarland classes, but does not give necessary and sufficient conditions for every vectorial bent $B$.

progress.summary: Question 1 asks which vectorial bent functions admit a nontrivial square extension with $2^n-2^m$ bent components.

A published construction gives vectorial Boolean functions with the maximum number of bent components beyond the Nyberg bound, covering a strict positive family rather than classifying all extendable vectorial bent functions.
